To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with RME (right mesial temporal lobar epilepsy) have reduced amygdala activity to fearful faces and reduced activity in the periaqueductral gray, which are both brain regions involved in the perception and regulation of emotion.
right mesial temporal lobar epilepsy impairs empathy related brain responses to dynamic faces.

patients with right mesial temporal lobar epilepsy (RMTLE), a common form of epilepsy, show reduced activity in the right amydgala and periaqueductral gray, brain regions that are crucial for the processing of interoceptive signals that are essential for the emotional awareness necessary for empathy.

the question of whether and how epilepsy affects the neural mechanisms that are responsible for the ability to understand others’ emotions.
